explanation: I found no Mathlib lemma that states this two-sided result. Mathlib has the two one-sided versions, `CochainComplex.isZero_of_isStrictlyGE` and `CochainComplex.isZero_of_isStrictlyLE`, both in `Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/Embedding/CochainComplex.lean`. The library's proof splits into cases and applies each of them once, so it combines two Mathlib results. That is more than a single-declaration instantiation. Searches: I grepped `Mathlib/Algebra/Homology` for `Icc`, which turned up only unrelated `IsStrictlyGE a`/`IsStrictlyLE b` statements in `DerivedCategory/Fractions.lean` and `DerivedCategory/TStructure.lean`. I grepped all of Mathlib for `isZero_*` lemmas mentioning `isStrictly`, `notMem` or `not_mem`, and for declarations that take both `IsStrictlyGE` and `IsStrictlyLE` instances. The only match with both instances was `exists_iso_single`, which is a different statement. I also checked `isZero_X_of_isStrictlySupported` in `Embedding/IsSupported.lean`. It is stated for a general embedding, and Mathlib has no `Icc`-shaped embedding of ℤ to apply it to.
